title: Right-pinched coherent nerve mapping sets are the Q-singular complex
statement:
Use small simplicial categories, the inclusion-ordered-subset coherent realization $\mathfrak C$, and its right adjoint $N_{\mathrm{hc}}$ from [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison]. Use $J^n=(\Delta^n\star\{y\})\amalg_{\Delta^n}\{x\}$, $Q^n=\mathfrak C[J^n](x,y)$ and $\operatorname{Sing}_Q$ from [lem-coef-pinched-rigidification-resolution]. Let $A$ be any small simplicial category and $x,y$ any two objects, possibly equal. Set $P=N_{\mathrm{hc}}A$ and $T=A(x,y)$. Define $M_A(x,y)_n$ to be the set of maps $\Delta^{n+1}\to P$ constant at $x$ on the entire initial face $\Delta^{\{0,\ldots,n\}}$ and taking the last vertex to $y$. Its simplicial operators extend $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$ by sending the new last vertex to the new last vertex. Equivalently these are maps $J^n\to P$ with the indicated vertices. There is a natural isomorphism of simplicial sets
$$\Phi_{A,x,y}:M_A(x,y)\xrightarrow{\cong}\operatorname{Sing}_Q T.$$
In degree $n$, it sends $z:J^n\to P$ to the morphism map $Q^n\to A(x,y)$ of the enriched adjoint $\mathfrak C[J^n]\to A$; its inverse is the coherent-nerve adjoint of the enriched functor with the displayed object images and that specified morphism map. This description is natural under simplicial functors of $A$ and under every face and degeneracy in $n$. No local Kan hypothesis is required; when $A$ is locally Kan, $M_A(x,y)$ is the right-pinched mapping space of $P$ in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones].

source.place: Sections 1.1.5 (coherent realization/nerve adjunction) and 2.2.2 (the pinched simplex J and Q), and opening of Section 2.2.4 (right mapping spaces of a coherent nerve). Agent-explicit adjunction identification, with inclusion-ordered subsets as in Arakawa, Levelwise nerves of simplicial categories, p.31. No Stacks tag states this simplicial enriched identification; read online, archive WANTED.

proof.text: Distinguish the vertices $a,b$ of $J^n$ from their prescribed images $x,y$ in $A$. The pushout defining $J^n$ identifies maps $J^n\to P$ with maps $\Delta^{n+1}\to P$ constant at $x$ on the entire initial face and with last vertex $y$: this is exactly its universal property, degree by degree. Apply the natural adjunction $\mathfrak C\dashv N_{\mathrm{hc}}$ to obtain a bijection with enriched functors $G:\mathfrak C[J^n]\to A$ satisfying $G(a)=x,G(b)=y$. Vertex restrictions correspond under this bijection because the coherent realization of a vertex has one object and only its identity. Restricting $G$ to $(a,b)$ defines $\Phi_n(z):Q^n\to T$.

source.place: Definitions 1.1.5.1, 1.1.5.5; Example 2.2.2.5; proof preceding Proposition 2.2.2.13, printed p.78.

proof.text: Let $r_n:\Delta^{n+1}\to J^n$ be the quotient. For $0\leq i\leq n$ put $H_i=\mathfrak C[\Delta^{n+1}](i,n+1)$ and let $q_i:H_i\to Q^n$ be the mapping map of $\mathfrak C[r_n]$. This functor sends every mapping simplex between initial vertices to the identity of $a$: its restriction factors through $\mathfrak C[\Delta^0]$. Consequently for $i\leq j\leq n$, union composition satisfies $q_i(U\cup V)=q_j(V)$ on $\mathfrak C[\Delta^{n+1}](i,j)\times H_j$. Given $t:Q^n\to T$, define an enriched functor $F_t:\mathfrak C[\Delta^{n+1}]\to A$ by sending all initial vertices to $x$, the last to $y$, all initial mapping sets constantly to $1_x$, the last endomorphism to $1_y$, and $H_i$ by $tq_i$. Empty reverse mapping sets have their unique maps. Its composition laws are precisely the displayed union identity and the unit laws of $A$; its identity laws are the same unit laws. Thus $F_t$ is an enriched functor whose initial restriction is the constant functor at $x$.

source.place: Definition 1.1.5.1 (union composition), Example 2.2.2.5, and proof of Proposition 2.2.2.13; explicit construction of the inverse.

proof.text: The maps $q_i$ jointly cover $Q^n=\mathfrak C[J^n](a,b)$ in every simplicial degree. Let $D\subseteq\mathfrak C[J^n]$ be the simplicial subcategory with objects $a,b$, only identities as endomorphisms, empty mapping set from $b$ to $a$, and $D(a,b)=\bigcup_iq_i(H_i)$, a simplicial subset because each $q_i$ is simplicial. Its only composites are unit composites, so it is closed under composition. By step 2, $\mathfrak C[r_n]$ sends initial mapping sets to $1_a$, the last endomorphism to $1_b$ and $H_i$ into $q_i(H_i)$, so $\mathfrak C[r_n]=\iota E$ with $\iota:D\to\mathfrak C[J^n]$ the inclusion and $E:\mathfrak C[\Delta^{n+1}]\to D$ constant at $1_a$ on the initial face. The coherent-nerve transpose of $E$ restricts on $\Delta^n$ to the transpose of a functor factoring through $\mathfrak C[\Delta^0]$, i.e. the degenerate simplex at $a$; by the pushout defining $J^n$ it descends along $r_n$ to $w:J^n\to N_{\mathrm{hc}}D$. Let $W:\mathfrak C[J^n]\to D$ be its adjoint; naturality of the adjunction gives $W\mathfrak C[r_n]=E$, hence $\iota W\mathfrak C[r_n]=\mathfrak C[r_n]$. The simplices $J^n\to N_{\mathrm{hc}}\mathfrak C[J^n]$ adjoint to $\iota W$ and to the identity therefore agree after precomposition with the degreewise surjection $r_n$, so they are equal and $\iota W$ is the identity functor. Hence $\iota$ is surjective on the mapping set $(a,b)$: every simplex of $Q^n$ is $q_i$ of a simplex of $H_i$ for some $i$.

source.place: Proof preceding Proposition 2.2.2.13, printed p.78 ("this is simply the data of a map of simplicial sets Q^n -> Map_C(x,y)"): generation of C[J^n](x,y) by the images of the coherent-simplex mapping sets, written out via the adjunction and the pushout J^n.

proof.text: Transpose $F_t$ under the coherent-nerve adjunction. Its initial restriction is constant, so the resulting simplex descends uniquely along $r_n$ to $z_t:J^n\to P$ with the specified vertices. Let $G_t$ be its adjoint. Naturality of adjunction gives $G_t\mathfrak C[r_n]=F_t$, hence $(G_t)_{a,b}q_i=tq_i$ for every $i$. The degreewise covering in step 3 implies $(G_t)_{a,b}=t$, so $\Phi_n(z_t)=t$. Conversely, if $t=G_{a,b}$ for the adjoint of $z$, the restriction $G\mathfrak C[r_n]$ agrees with $F_t$ on every object and mapping set: the initial ones are identities, the final endomorphism is the identity, and on $H_i$ it is $tq_i$. Their adjoint simplices agree, and uniqueness in the pushout gives $z_t=z$. Thus these formulas are inverse bijections. At $n=0$ they send an edge exactly to its vertex in $T$, since $J^0=\Delta^1$ and $Q^0=\Delta^0$.

source.place: Example 2.2.2.5 and proof of Proposition 2.2.2.13, printed p.78; both inverse identities expanded.

proof.text: For any monotone $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$, extend it by $\bar\alpha(m+1)=n+1$. This preserves the initial faces and last vertices and gives $j_\alpha:J^m\to J^n$. By the definitions its realized $(a,b)$ mapping map is $Q(\alpha):Q^m\to Q^n$. If $G$ is adjoint to $z$, the functor adjoint to $zj_\alpha$ is $G\mathfrak C[j_\alpha]$. Restricting to $(a,b)$ therefore gives the equality $\Phi_m(zj_\alpha)=\Phi_n(z)\,Q(\alpha)$, exactly the simplicial operator in $\operatorname{Sing}_QT$. This holds for all monotone maps, including noninjective ones. Hence the bijections assemble into a simplicial map; their inverses commute with operators by applying this equality and bijectivity in each degree. They form the asserted simplicial isomorphism.

source.place: Proposition 2.2.2.13, naturality with respect to [n]; direct-image cosimplicial operators in Section 2.2.2, printed pp.76,78.

proof.text: For a simplicial functor $u:A\to A'$, the simplex $N_{\mathrm{hc}}(u)z$ is adjoint to $uG$. Taking its $(a,b)$ mapping map yields $\Phi_{A',u(x),u(y),n}(N_{\mathrm{hc}}(u)z)=u_{x,y}\Phi_{A,x,y,n}(z)$. Postcomposition on the right is precisely $\operatorname{Sing}_Q(u_{x,y})$. This proves naturality in $A$ and in the displayed pair of objects, including functors that identify objects. All the constructions above use identities and composition, so they also apply when $x=y$; no condition on the mapping simplicial sets was used.

source.place: Proposition 2.2.2.13: natural isomorphism, and its adjunction proof; target-functor naturality written explicitly.

proof.text: If $A$ is locally Kan, the cited coherent-nerve theorem gives that $P=N_{\mathrm{hc}}A$ is a quasicategory. The definition of its right-pinched mapping space in the enhanced-diagram definition is exactly the formula for $M_A(x,y)$, including the entire constant initial face and the extension of operators by the last vertex. Thus $M_A(x,y)$ is that mapping space. This last interpretation is the only use of local Kan; the isomorphism already proved holds for arbitrary small simplicial $A$.

source.place: Proposition 1.1.5.10 for the quasicategory assertion; Proposition 2.2.2.13 for the mapping identification; project right-pinched convention in def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones.
